Georgia Ports Authority Backs UNP-NSC Merger, Boosting Connectivity
sum: Union Pacific Corporation UNP and Norfolk Southern Corporation NSC continue to gain support for their proposed merger, with the Georgia Ports Authority becoming the latest major transportation stakeholder to endorse the transaction. The backing adds to a growing coalition of more than 2,000 businesses, labor organizations, public officials and industry associations that believe the combination could strengthen the U.S. freight transportation network.

The proposed merger aims to create the nation's first seamless transcontinental railroad, connecting Georgia's major ports with a wider range of inland markets through a single-line rail network. This could expand shipping options for manufacturers, exporters and distributors while improving access to domestic and international markets. The Port of Savannah, North America's largest single-terminal container facility, and the Port of Brunswick, the country's leading gateway for automobiles and heavy machinery, could benefit from stronger rail connectivity.

The combination could also build on existing infrastructure investments, including the Gainesville Inland Port, which currently relies exclusively on Norfolk Southern for rail services. An expanded network could increase the reach of inland terminals, provide customers access to more destinations and create additional opportunities for businesses moving goods across the country. These improvements could further support Georgia's growing role in international trade and logistics.

Overall, the Georgia Ports Authority's endorsement strengthens the case for the proposed merger, particularly in terms of freight connectivity, market access and supply-chain efficiency. However, the transaction remains subject to regulatory approval, and its long-term benefits will depend on how effectively the combined railroad integrates operations and delivers the promised service improvements.
UNP's and NSC's shares have gained 29% and 13.1%, respectively, over the year-to-date period compared with the Transportation - Rail industry's 28.4% growth.

Can Union Pacific (NYSE:UNP) Keep Its Record Growth on Track?
sum: - Operating revenue rose notably, and net earnings rose notably.
- Union Pacific affirmed guidance for high-single-digit growth in posted earnings per share for the year and pricing gains ahead of inflation.
- The company posted records for freight revenue, freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge, operating revenue, operating earnings and net earnings.

Union Pacific reports record freight and operating revenue, supported by higher shipment volumes, pricing gains and improved operational efficiency, while reaffirming its full-year growth guidance and capital expenditure plans.

Operating revenue rose notably. Union Pacific attributed the increase to a higher fuel surcharge, a notable share volume growth, core pricing gains and higher other revenue, partly offset by business mix. Freight revenue excluding fuel surcharge, a measure that strips out the pass-through effect of fuel costs, increased notably. Revenue carloads, the railroad's basic unit of volume, grew notably. That growth matters for a network business, because additional carloads moving across the same track, terminals and crews can spread fixed costs over a larger base, which is why railroads track carload growth so closely from multi-quarter to the next.

The posted operating ratio, which expresses operating expenses as a share of operating revenue and where a lower figure indicates greater efficiency, came in at a notable level, an improvement of multiple basis points from the prior year. The adjusted operating ratio was a notable level.

Alongside the financial figures, Union Pacific posted a series of operating measures that it uses to track service and efficiency. Freight car velocity, which counts the average daily miles a car travels, reached numerous miles per day, up notably. Average terminal dwell, the time a car spends in a rail yard, improved a notable share to multiple hours. Together, these figures show the railroad absorbing a notable share more volume while moving cars through its yards faster and running longer, more fuel-efficient trains.

sum: Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE:UNP) Industrials Union Pacific Corporation (NYSE:UNP) 289.33 USD +2.035 0.708% Last Updated at: 2026-11-23T20:58:00Z said it looks forward to a full evaluation of its proposed merger with Norfolk Southern after the deadline for public comments on the deal passed this week. For readers who follow Infrastructure and Real Estate stocks, this merger is one of the most significant transportation infrastructure deals in decades. Union Pacific trades on the NYSE Composite.

Union Pacific agreed to acquire Norfolk Southern in a deal valued at tens of billions of dollars. Union Pacific operates one of the largest railroad networks in the western United States, while Norfolk Southern serves the eastern half of the country. Today, freight moving across the country must be handed off between railroads in the middle of the nation, often in Chicago or other gateways.
A combined network would allow shipments to travel coast to coast on a single railroad, which the companies say would cut delivery times by a day or two for many shipments.

The Surface Transportation Board, the federal agency that oversees railroads, rejected the companies' first application earlier this year as incomplete. The railroads filed a revised application, which the board accepted but paused while requesting additional information.

After the railroads submitted supplemental information, the board removed the proceeding from abeyance and set a schedule for evaluating the merits of the deal. Comments from shippers, other railroads, unions and the public were due this week. The board has also denied requests from opponents to dismiss the application.

After the comment period, the railroads will respond to concerns, and the board will continue its detailed review of competition, service, safety and public benefits. A final decision is expected next year. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern expect the transaction to close in the second half of next year if approved.

Union Pacific stock: BNSF urges STB to reject merger
sum: BNSF filed comments with the Surface Transportation Board on Wednesday, November 18, urging the regulator to reject the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger. The filing adds a new set of objections and requested safeguards as the regulatory review moves through stakeholder submissions.

BNSF said the combination would harm competition and customers, arguing that projected growth and operating benefits are overstated. It said the applicants' proposed gateway pricing, targeted access and rate-arbitration measures would not adequately address the risks identified in its filing.

The railroad proposed access for BNSF trains on Norfolk Southern track between Chicago and Pennsylvania, together with access to Norfolk Southern intermodal terminals. BNSF said the measures would preserve a competing option for shipments moving between West Coast ports and the Northeast.

For the Gulf Coast, BNSF requested a neutral terminal railroad connecting customers with both Union Pacific and BNSF. It also proposed a permanent interline preservation mechanism covering all traffic, affected customers and existing interchange points, with rates linked to an objective benchmark and transitional protection for current gateway rates.

BNSF further requested open access for facilities served by only one railroad when they are within 20 miles of an active interchange with another major railroad. The proposal includes cost-based switching fees, annual updates and service standards overseen by an independent compliance monitor.

Additional requests cover shared rail resources and key hubs. BNSF said Union Pacific should keep its ownership of the TTX railcar pool below 50 percent, while it also called for protections involving New Orleans, Memphis and the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and Kansas City Terminal Railway.

items.t: Union Pacific (UNP) Stock Rises 1.30% on Wednesday, Up 4.5% in a Month
sum: Technical analysis of UNP stock on November 18, 2026: price 300.90 USD, trend uptrend, RSI 54.3, support 290.16, resistance 308.53.

Union Pacific shares closed at $300.90 on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, a 1.30% advance that lifted the railroad operator back above its 20-day moving average — and, just as notably, back inside striking distance of a three-month high of $314.15. The move matters less for its size than for its position: after a five-session drift of −0.40%, the stock is again doing the work of an uptrend, and the last session's volume of 3.07 million shares, roughly 1.0× the 20-day average of 2.94 million, confirms that buyers, not a thin tape, did the lifting.

What makes UNP worth watching now is the combination of a slow-building price recovery and a volatility squeeze, a setup that historically resolves in a decisive move. Over the past month the stock has gained 4.53%, and the 20-day average has risen 1.15% over five days, a measured upward drift rather than a spike.

The structural picture is constructive. UNP trades above both its 20-day average of $300.33 and its 50-day average of $288.05, with the 20-day average itself above the 50-day — the classic geometry of an established uptrend. No fresh moving-average cross has formed, which is a good thing: the trend is mature rather than freshly minted, and there is no crossover signal to fade. As shown in the chart, price sits at 58% of its 20-day range, between support at $290.16 and resistance at $308.53, having already absorbed the pullback into the 20-day average that the prior week's −0.40% reading implied. That pullback, held within an uptrend, is precisely the pattern the selection signals flag as bullish.

The Bollinger setup is the sharper story. Band width has compressed to 5.8%, a squeeze that tells you the market has temporarily agreed on a price and is waiting for a reason to disagree. The upper band at $309.06 and lower band at $291.60 are unusually tight around the 20-day mean, and %B at 53% puts price in the middle of that envelope — coiled, not extended.

Momentum is the one place where the bullish case has a visible crack. RSI(14) at 54.3 is squarely neutral, neither overbought nor oversold, and Stochastic readings of 56.2 (fast) against 54.5 (slow) are similarly non-committal.

The report draws on historical examples to justify its argument. During the automobile revolution, car manufacturers appeared to be the obvious initial beneficiaries. However, their long-term returns were limited by intense competition and industry consolidation. Meanwhile, companies such as the Walton family's retail giant capitalized on the broader shifts enabled by automobiles, including suburbanization and expansion of big-box retail.

Similarly, the widespread adoption of Wi-Fi did not necessarily translate into exceptional returns for router manufacturers, while Netflix emerged as a clear winner from the subsequent growth of streaming. Morgan Stanley believes that AI could follow a similar pattern, with AI-driven automation and productive workforces representing a similar second-order investment opportunity.

To identify potential winners, the firm developed an indicator called the AI Productivity Spread, calculated by subtracting the growth in average technical employee compensation from the growth in revenue per technical employee. A positive and widening spread suggests that the organization is particularly effective at translating AI adoption into higher employee productivity and business output.

Coal from the company's North Antelope Rochelle Mine traveled on Union Pacific's network to Nogales, Arizona, where it was handed to Mexican railroad Ferromex for the final run to the port in Sonora. From there it was loaded onto a Panamax-sized vessel and shipped to Vietnam, which Peabody told investors at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference arrived on time and to specification.

The move demonstrates that the route works, not that it is commercially viable. Union Pacific and Peabody have described the shipments as a feasibility test, and the railroad says future runs will depend on market conditions. North Antelope Rochelle, about 65 miles south of Gillette, produced 65 million short tons of coal in 2025 and is served by both Union Pacific and BNSF. Union Pacific has also been investing in battery-electric locomotives across its wider network.
Guaymas Handled Less Cargo in 2025 Than Its Own Operating Plan

Port capacity is the first open question. Mexico's port authority ASIPONA recorded 5.01 million tonnes of total cargo at Guaymas in 2025, down 5% from 5.25 million tonnes in 2024 and roughly 35% short of the port's own operating plan of 7.65 million tonnes. Its commercial handbook advertises total operating capacity of 14.2 million tonnes, a port-wide figure covering all cargo types, not a coal-specific one, and it lists no dedicated coal terminal. Modernization projects covering mineral storage and a new multipurpose quay are underway, though the port has not published completion dates or coal-specific capacity targets.

A pilot shipment proves rail and port compatibility, but it says nothing about repeat capability. Recurring unit trains and ocean vessels require reliable unloading, storage, dust control and berth availability well beyond what one test run demonstrates.

Speaking to CNBC on Thursday, Vena said he's complimented by Trump's interest, but that Union Pacific doesn't need any such federal support. Trump in May told Fortune that he wants a 15% federal stake in the large railroad merger—although he didn't specifically name UP—comments that came just days before a federal regulator put the mega deal on pause for additional review.
"We're a company that can afford to make this deal," Vena said. "We're a company that can afford to handle what the price is for this deal, and we do not need anybody's help to do this."

"Listen, I have not had any direct communication with the president of the United States to talk about the president and the government specifically coming in and being a partner in this."

While Vena made it clear he considers federal intervention unnecessary, his remarks left open the potential to negotiate if the Trump administration presses the topic, possibly wanting to avoid antagonizing the president for now.

sum: Getting big returns from financial portfolios, whether through stocks, bonds, ETFs, other securities, or a combination of all, is an investor's dream. But for income investors, generating consistent cash flow from each of your liquid investments is your primary focus.

Cash flow can come from bond interest, interest from other types of investments, and, of course, dividends. A dividend is the distribution of a company's earnings paid out to shareholders; it's often viewed by its dividend yield, a metric that measures a dividend as a percent of the current stock price. Many academic studies show that dividends account for significant portions of long-term returns, with dividend contributions exceeding one-third of total returns in many cases.

Headquartered in Omaha, Union Pacific (UNP) is a Transportation stock that has seen a price change of 14.94% so far this year. Looking ahead, future dividend growth will be dependent on earnings growth and payout ratio, which is the proportion of a company's annual earnings per share that it pays out as a dividend. Investors like dividends for many reasons; they greatly improve stock investing profits, decrease overall portfolio risk, and carry tax advantages, among others. But, not every company offers a quarterly payout.

items.t: STB rejects Union Pacific – Norfolk Southern transcontinental railroad merger application as incomplete; what comes next?
sum: The Surface Transportation Board (“STB” or “Board”) last Friday rejected the application filed by Union Pacific Railroad Company (UP) and Norfolk Southern Railway Company (NS) for UP to acquire control of NS and merge their rail operations. See Decision, STB Docket No. FD 36873 (served Jan. 16, 2026). The STB determined that it had to reject the application because it did not contain the market share impact analyses or a full copy of the merger agreement (and related documents) as required by the STB's regulations. However, the Board's rejection was without prejudice to the right of the applicants to refile a new application which corrects these deficiencies.

The proposed combination of UP and NS is anticipated to have significant impacts for the rail industry and its various stakeholders, including other railroads, shippers, passenger rail systems, equipment providers, service providers, ports, and rail labor. Although we believe it is likely (but not certain) UP and NS will refile their application, the Board’s rejection decision provides interested stakeholders with a brief window of opportunity to assess (based on the initial application materials) how the proposed merger would impact their interests and whether they should participate in the STB merger review proceeding going forward if any revised application is filed and accepted by the Board as complete.
We have provided below our initial assessment of the key potential impacts of the proposed merger on various rail stakeholders.

- Other Railroads (including Short Lines). The other Class I railroads have all expressed public opposition to the proposed merger based on its alleged impacts on rail-to-rail competition and the combined railroad’s market power. The applicants (UP and NS) have stated in the application that short line railroads are likely to see increased traffic volume as a result of new single-line routes and traffic diverted from trucks. However, each short line will have to evaluate the potential competitive impact of the merger (especially in the areas where there is overlap between the UP and NS systems).
- Shippers.The applicants assert that shippers could see cheaper alternatives for transporting goods with lower overall costs.
